The full archived history includes regressions and incomplete runs. Independent unseen qualification is pending. No generalization, model-call reduction or wall-clock speedup claim.

video_selection: Three native development recordings of base seed 2 layout 11: R14, R17, R22. Same light striped shirt, clean wooden table, initial arrangement and head camera. Native scores 0, 20, 100; two failures followed by success. Chart values use the separate complete common 40-scene coverage cohort.
memory_note: Six documented mechanisms; all previews use development base seed 2 layout 11. R14 has motion feedback, not R13 return memory. R17 has feedback and return memory with reverse-descent-path withdrawal. R22 has R13 return poses, R19 wrist refinement and cross-view checks, R21 target selection, and R22 temporal association. R22 does not inherit R17 reverse-path withdrawal. Only present mechanisms are highlighted.

presentation.note: Missed right sleeve; both sleeves folded but one hem corner missed; complete native success. The two comparisons show the same right-sleeve action and the whole folding sequence.
presentation.task_goal: Fold both sleeves, then fold the hem up.

playlist.editing_note: Show the sleeve attempts through 15.4 seconds. The left motion displaces the shirt; the right grasp misses and that sleeve remains outside. Omit the unsuccessful hem attempt. Failed is the full native outcome, not a controller abort at the editorial cut.

memory_library.summary: Return to a pose reached earlier.
memory_library.description: Save the approach joint pose and return to it after releasing the cloth.

memory_library.summary: Follow the cloth as it folds.
memory_library.description: Match the folded cloth to its earlier position and outline before grasping the hem.

memory_library.summary: Match the wrist view to the garment.
memory_library.description: Accept a wrist grasp correction only where the wrist and head views both identify cloth.

presentation.narrative_note: R14 displaces the shirt during the left fold and misses the right sleeve. R17 uses recorded return poses and reverses its measured descent path: both sleeves fold in, but the left hem grasp misses. This precise development scene is cited in the R19 wrist-refinement SPEC. R22 inherits R19 wrist refinement, R21 shirt selection and R13 return poses, and adds temporal garment association; it completes the fold. R22 does not inherit the R17 reverse-path variant. These are selected campaign policies, not isolated ablations or a direct parent-child chain. Videos are development examples; SR and Score include all results in each separate complete common 40-scene chart cohort.

bridges.title: Right-sleeve grasp
bridges.action: right-sleeve grasp, lift, fold and release
bridges.mechanism: R17 inherits saved return poses and reverses the measured descent path after release. The shirt stays in place after the left fold; its right sleeve is then acquired. R14 and R17 differ in more than one control mechanism; this is not an isolated ablation.
bridges.narration: The right sleeve is missed. With return memory, both sleeves fold in.
bridges.visual_note: Both sides show the same action, camera, source interval, crop, speed schedule and holds. The first comparison follows right-sleeve acquisition through release. The second starts both recordings at zero and plays both to their native ends; the earlier-ending recording holds its terminal frame.
bridges.comparison_limit: The edit identifies specific visible problems and documented remedies, not the sole cause of a complete episode score. R14, R17 and R22 are selected campaign policies with different control lineages. The full-task comparison contains multiple changes and is not an isolated ablation.

sequence.narration_note: Synthetic English narration is embedded only in the two bridges. Muted autoplay; the speaker button enables it. Audio follows pause, seek and speed.
sequence.editing_note: R14 is editorially cut at 15.4 seconds after the right-sleeve failure; this is not a controller abort. R17 and R22 keep their entire action sequences. Repeated sleeves play at 3×, final folds at 1×, with 0.8-second outcome holds. Each comparison synchronizes the same action phase from both policies, with the same camera, crop and speed schedule within each pair. Repeated actions are accelerated with visible speed labels; final folds play at native speed. Attempt footage retains its full frame. No generated, stabilized or interpolated robot motion.
